classification.difficultyReason: Use the first two scaffolded vector calculations, then construct NS and recognise that it is four times NM to establish collinearity.

content.prompt:
PQR is a triangle with $\underset{\sim}{x}$, $\underset{\sim}{y}$ and $2\underset{\sim}{y}$ as shown.

N is a point on QP, such that $QN=2NP$.

R is the midpoint of QS.

M is the midpoint of PR.

spec.description: Q, R and S are collinear with QR=RS. Triangle QPR has N on QP and M on PR. Rightward QR arrow is x; QN and NP arrows point towards P and are labelled 2y and y. No NS line is supplied.
spec.mathematics: QN=2NP; PM=MR; QR=RS; vector QR=x, vector QN=2y, vector NP=y.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent question figure; the requested straight line NMS is not drawn.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Show that NMS is a straight line.

answer.short: $\overrightarrow{NS}=4\overrightarrow{NM}$. These vectors are parallel and share N, so N, M and S are collinear.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{NS}&=\overrightarrow{NQ}+\overrightarrow{QS}\\\overrightarrow{NS}&=-2\underset{\sim}{y}+2\underset{\sim}{x}\\\overrightarrow{NS}&=-2(\underset{\sim}{y}-\underset{\sim}{x})\\\overrightarrow{NM}&=-\tfrac12\underset{\sim}{y}+\tfrac12\underset{\sim}{x}\\\overrightarrow{NM}&=-\tfrac12(\underset{\sim}{y}-\underset{\sim}{x})\\\overrightarrow{NS}&=4\overrightarrow{NM}\end{aligned}$$
The vectors $\overrightarrow{NM}$ and $\overrightarrow{NS}$ are parallel and share the common point N. Therefore N, M and S are collinear.
